title: IonQ prices $40 per unit offering with 20.5M shares, 29.5M pre-funded warrants and 100M Series C warrants
source_used: TradingView (relaying IonQ's 8-K of 16 Oct 2026); AWP Alliance News brief on vermoegenszentrum.ch; Quantum Computing Report (14 Oct pricing)
key_facts: IonQ filed an 8-K with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on 16 Oct 2026 about an underwriting deal to sell 20,500,000 shares, 29,500,000 pre-funded warrants and 100,000,000 Series C warrants at a combined price of $40.00 per unit.
AWP Alliance News (an AI-generated brief based on the filing) says IonQ closed the offering on 16 Oct 2026.
Each share or pre-funded warrant came with two Series C warrants, which gives the 100,000,000 Series C warrants.
The Series C warrants have an exercise price of $69.46 per share; the pre-funded warrants carry an exercise price of $0.0001 per share.
Both warrant types can be exercised immediately and expire on the seventh anniversary of issuance.

Quantum Computing Report (14 Oct 2026): the offering was priced at $2.0 billion, bought directly from the underwriter by an investment entity managed by Heights Capital Management, at a 15% premium to the 13 Oct close of $34.78.
IonQ plans to use the proceeds to accelerate commercialization, manufacturing and deployment of its quantum platform across computing, networking, sensing and cybersecurity.
quote_evidence: IonQ entered an underwriting deal to sell 20,500,000 shares, 29,500,000 pre-funded warrants and 100,000,000 Series C warrants at a combined price of $40.00 per unit.
IonQ closed its securities offering on October 16, 2026.
Each share or pre-funded warrant was offered with two Series C Warrants at a combined public price of USD 40.
why_it_matters_hint: The roughly $2 billion raise is now complete, and the warrants could add up to 100 million new shares if used.
event_date: Offering priced 14 Oct 2026; closed and 8-K filed 16 Oct 2026
notes: TradingView text is only two sentences, so the closing date and warrant terms come from the AWP Alliance News brief, which says it was generated by AI from the EDGAR filing; the SEC filing itself returned 403 and was not opened (the index link comes from that brief). The pricing and buyer come from Quantum Computing Report. Follow-up of the 15 Oct 2026 edition item (1015:C15-03) on the pricing.
